changelog: [When to Segment]: added a bullet that treats the position right after a clause's governing predicate, conditional ending (-으면/-면), or reporting/hedging verb (같다/말하다/보다/생각하다) as a high-value candidate boundary once it has surfaced — this gives the ranking step a concrete 'safe' position to prefer over early NP-only cuts, addressing placement failures where fragments before the governing verb were emitted and later contradicted.

[Priority Rules]: inserted a new rank-3 tier for boundaries right after a surfaced governing/conditional/reporting/hedging verb (safer than -거든/-잖아/-니까), added a balanced-split criterion (prefer boundaries that divide a clause roughly evenly over ones stranding most content in one piece, fixing the priority failures where filler-adjacent or earliest cuts left oversized remainders), and — instead of forbidding them outright as the previous rejected revision did — demoted bare NP/subjectless-verb/embedded-clause-before-governing-verb boundaries and isolated-interjection boundaries to low ranks so they are still marked (available under loose budgets) but dropped first under tight ones.
